cells.tense: The seeing is whole, and the hand is resting at the edge of the page, done writing.
cells.act: reason it from first principles once
cells.ask: Take a question you can see all the way through, and reason it once from its start to its end. No plan after, no decision. The line, held whole.
cells.core:
In your practice, some questions have thinned to something you can hold — the shape, where it starts, what it's made of, where it goes. Returning to a thing alone until it stops being hard can arrive at exactly this.

What's useful now is to run one of those through once from first principles, all the way, then leave it alone. No plan, no decision after. You keep the depth. What changes is that the thing doesn't have to keep earning its place. The cost of holding this is giving up the comfort of a question still open — the view is finished, and finished views don't get to be surprising.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it whole. You don't have to keep deciding.
cells.verb: seeing a thing all the way through until nothing in it is hidden
cells.place: in a practice you return to alone, where repetition turns intention into skill

cells.tense: You are running toward the end of every question, and the page is finished before you sit down.
cells.act: let the impulse start without a plan
cells.ask: Before you decide what something means, let it start — a line, a question, a page. No plan for what it becomes. Just that first minute.
cells.core:
In your practice, conclusions are assembling while the middle is still going. The pattern shows up fast, the ending is decided before the thing has had a chance to be itself, and the front — where it's still nothing in particular — is the part being skipped.

Before deciding what anything is, let it start with no plan. Something you've already concluded about: let a minute of it begin again, pointed nowhere. You don't have to know what it is. That's the whole thing. The first spark doesn't need a target, and you can be present at the moment it catches, which is something your fast seeing skips. The depth you have stays with you.
cells.sheetLine: You know the ending before the thing has started.

cells.tense: A question closed, and you are standing at a door your feet have already passed.
cells.act: decide what this is for before you spend it
cells.ask: Name in one line what your practice is for right now — not how, what it serves — then do the next session toward that line and nothing else.
cells.core:
The repetition is still running in your practice and the direction has gone quiet. The sitting, the drills, the hours — kept, without a line leading them. Choosing the line is the step not being taken, and it's the one that would make the hours mean something again.

Back up one step: name what the practice is for, in a line, then take the next session toward that name alone. You don't have to force old effort back into the room. Deciding the line is what pulls the current. If no line comes, that absence is honest, and a line can be decided from it. Pick the form first, then spend.
cells.sheetLine: The hours kept going after you stopped choosing.

cells.tense: This clarity is already running, and you keep saying it happens to you.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: In the middle of practice today, pause once and catch one thing that wasn't here a minute ago — a sound, a word that shifted. Then continue.
cells.core:
The pattern shows up before you say it, the line is followed without deciding to follow it, and the account afterward is that it happened to you — luck, talent, something in the air. The one it happens to is the one doing it. The story leaves that one standing outside the practice.

Today, mid-session, stop once and catch something newly here — a sound, a word that shifted, a page that turned — then go on. You're not proving anything; you're looking at the moment from the side it comes in on. The line runs by your hand, and that hand is yours. Caught once, the practice stops happening to you.
cells.sheetLine: The clarity is yours, and you keep leaving yourself out.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the opening of the Balanced core — that a person would recognise a want to hand the seeing over rather than keep deciding alone; the record says the capacity is integrated, not that it is spent. The reader might reasonably say the seeing is not yet total, that a part is still hidden, and my read is 'finished' when their process is still running. The ask survives: sitting with one thing already known, keeping your hands out, is useful whether the process is complete or simply ready to be handed on once. The sentence that serves me more than them is the first clause about wanting to hand it over — cut it, and the Balanced core opens on the both-and it is actually about.
